title: What if Yellowstone's supervolcano erupted?
lines: Ash would fall on most of America.
What if Yellowstone's supervolcano erupted today?
Its biggest eruption was about two thousand five hundred times bigger than Mount Saint Helens.
That's enough rock and ash to bury all of Texas eleven feet deep.
Now the ground [tears](tairs) open across a crater the size of Rhode Island.
Glowing avalanches of rock and gas race out, hot enough to melt aluminum.
Then the ash spreads in every direction, even against the [wind](wind).
Billings, Montana could get over three feet. Taller than a kitchen counter.
The Midwest, a few inches. New York and Miami, a dusting.
And ash isn't soft. It's jagged bits of rock and glass.
About four inches can cave in weak roofs.
It can melt inside jet engines and make them stall.
Sulfur gas would dim the Sun and cool the planet for years.
Probably by up to one and a half degrees Celsius. About twice Pinatubo's cooling.
But here's the good news. Yellowstone is not overdue.
The odds are about one in seven hundred thirty thousand a year. Like a big asteroid hitting Earth.
Only about a fifth of its magma is melted. It likely needs at least a third to erupt.
Its next eruption will most likely be a steam blast or a lava flow.
But if the big one ever came,
